title: Step sizes and optimizers
sub: Gradient descent on a 1-D bowl with three learning rates, then three optimizers on a narrow 2-D valley.

frames.caption: Start at w = -3.5, loss 12.25. Each step moves by −η × slope.
Twelve steps and still far from the bottom: each step shrinks w by only 10%. Safe, but painfully slow.
Start at w = -3.5, loss 12.25. Each step moves by −η × slope.
Each step multiplies w by 1 − 2η = 0.2: the loss collapses toward 0 in a few steps, overshooting slightly and settling.
Start at w = -1, loss 1. Each step moves by −η × slope.
Each step overshoots to the other side, further up than it started: w is multiplied by 1 − 2η = −1.1 every step. The loss grows forever. On this bowl, any η above 2/L = 1 diverges.
A long, narrow valley (25× steeper across than along), tilted. Three optimizers start at the same point, aiming for the center.
Plain gradient descent (orange) zigzags across the steep walls: the gradient mostly points across the valley, not along it, so progress along the valley is slow.
Momentum (blue) keeps a fraction of its previous step. Its first swings are big, but they die out fast while the along-the-valley motion keeps adding up: loss 0.25 already, versus 1.8 for plain GD.
Adam (green) divides each coordinate's step by the size of its recent gradients, so the steep and shallow directions get comparable steps.
Loss after 30 steps: plain 0.074, momentum 6.9e-08, Adam 0.1.

After 60 steps: plain GD 0.00095, momentum 9.8e-17, Adam 0.016. Well-tuned momentum wins on this clean bowl; Adam's fixed step makes it jitter near the bottom. Adam's real strength is needing little tuning across millions of directions with wildly different curvature.
